abstract.t: This document describes the Namespace Identifier (NID) 'mplify' for Uniform Resource Names (URNs) used to identify resources published by Mplify Alliance. Mplify specifies and manages resources that utilize this URN identification model. This URN namespace will complement the existing "mef" URN namespace registered in RFC 7818. Management activities for these and other resource types are handled by the manager of the Mplify Assigned Names and Numbers (MANN) registry.

section.title: Introduction
section.t: Mplify Alliance (https://www.mplify.net/), formerly MEF Forum, is a global alliance of enterprises, service providers, cloud providers, data center operators, technology providers, and systems integrators, working together to accelerate the AI-powered digital economy through standardization, automation, certification, and collaboration.

Mplify is the defining body for Carrier Ethernet, Lifecycle Service Orchestration (LSO) APIs, and certified SASE and SD-WAN. Mplify has developed the global blueprint for Network-as-a-Service (NaaS) that is empowering the industry to innovate, interoperate, and scale trusted network services across a global ecosystem.

In June 2025, MEF Forum became Mplify Alliance. The "mplify" URN namespace is being registered to provide persistent, unique identifiers for resources published under the Mplify Alliance brand, complementing the existing "mef" URN namespace registered in URN Namespace for MEF Documents. To ensure that this namespace's uniqueness is absolute, a registration of a specific Uniform Resource Name (URN) Uniform Resource Names (URNs) Namespace Identifier (NID) for use by Mplify is being specified in this document.

The existing "mef" URN namespace remains valid. URNs previously assigned under "urn:mef:*" continue to be valid and will not be reassigned or retired. No new assignments will be made under "mef". Apart from the exception for YANG modules described in , new resources, and new versions of resources previously identified under "mef", will be assigned URNs under the "mplify" namespace. A resource is never identified by both a "mef" and an "mplify" URN.

li.t: The "mplify" namespace identifies resources published by Mplify Alliance. These include:

ul.li: any other resources that require managed, persistent identification as part of Mplify Alliance activities.

li.t: The scope of the namespace is global. URNs in this namespace are used by service providers, enterprises, technology vendors, and other organizations that implement Mplify specifications, for example as identifiers in LSO API payloads and in YANG-based network management. A formal namespace gives these implementers persistent, globally unique identifiers that cannot collide with identifiers defined by other organizations. Software that implements Mplify specifications uses the URNs as identifiers and does not need to resolve them.

The namespace complements the "mef" namespace , which identifies resources published before the "mplify" namespace was registered. The relationship between the two namespaces is described under "Assignment" and "Interoperability" below. No resolution service is defined for the namespace (see "Resolution" below). URNs in this namespace are used in Mplify Alliance standards; the namespace is not part of an IETF standard.
The syntax of namespace-specific strings (NSSs) for the "mplify" namespace is <NSS> as defined in .

The NSS is hierarchical, with segments separated by colons. The first segment identifies a resource class, such as "lso" or "yang". The structure below the first segment is defined for each resource class and documented in the MANN registry.

Resources that are published in versions, such as LSO product specifications, have a separate URN for each version. The NSS of that URN contains a version segment consisting of the letter "v" followed by three non-negative integers separated by periods (major.minor.patch), for example "v2.0.0". The version segment may be followed by further segments that identify parts of that version. For such resources, an NSS without the version segment (for example, "lso:spec:sonata:access-eline-ovc") is a level in the registry hierarchy and does not itself identify a resource.
In addition to the URN-equivalence rules in , the entire URN, including the NSS, is case-insensitive. Mplify Alliance will not assign two URNs that differ only in case.

There are no special character encoding rules and no special considerations for conformance with the URN syntax. This registration does not define semantics for r-components, q-components, or f-components; they are therefore undefined for this namespace.

URNs in the "mplify" namespace are assigned by Mplify Alliance, which is the authority for the namespace. Assignment is not open to the public: URNs are assigned as part of the publication of Mplify Alliance specifications, standards, data models, and certification programs, in accordance with the procedures that Mplify Alliance defines for each resource class. Mplify Alliance may delegate assignment for specific resource classes to its working groups, committees, or partner organizations, but retains authority over the namespace.

Every assigned URN is recorded in the Mplify Assigned Names and Numbers (MANN) registry (https://www.mplify.net/MANN/), which Mplify Alliance uses to guarantee that each URN is unique. Once assigned, a URN is never reassigned to a different resource, even if the resource is deprecated or withdrawn.

URNs assigned under the "mef" namespace remain valid, are never reassigned, and are not re-issued under the "mplify" namespace. When a new version of a resource identified under "urn:mef:" is published, it is assigned a "urn:mplify:" URN whose NSS matches the NSS of the original except for the version segment, which continues the version numbering used under "mef".

YANG modules are an exception. does not allow the namespace of a published module to change, so a module whose namespace was assigned under "urn:mef:yang:" keeps that namespace in all later revisions. Only new YANG modules are assigned "urn:mplify:yang:" namespaces.
There are no additional security considerations other than those normally associated with the use and resolution of URNs in general, which are described in .

URNs in the "mplify" namespace identify publicly available specifications, data models, and related resources. The URNs do not contain personal or otherwise private information, and Mplify Alliance does not assign URNs based on information that could be used to track individuals. Because the identified resources are public, directory harvesting is not a concern.

URNs in the "mef" and "mplify" namespaces are never URN-equivalent (), and no version of a resource is identified in both namespaces. A "urn:mplify:" URN that differs from a "urn:mef:" URN only in its NID and version segment identifies a later version of the same resource; the MANN registry records this lineage. Software that relies on exact URN matching treats the two URNs as distinct identifiers.

ul.li: No resolution mechanism is intended or anticipated for this namespace at this time, and Mplify Alliance does not operate or recommend a resolution service. Information about the resources identified by "urn:mplify:" URNs is published in the MANN registry (https://www.mplify.net/MANN/). No semantics are defined for r-components.

Mplify Alliance publishes information about assigned URNs in the MANN registry (https://www.mplify.net/MANN/) and publishes its specifications at https://www.mplify.net/. The "mef" namespace is documented in .

Mplify Alliance was known as MEF Forum until June 2025, and the "mef" namespace was registered under that name. The "mplify" namespace reflects the new organizational identity while preserving the validity and persistence of all existing "urn:mef:" assignments. The MANN registry is the authoritative source for assignments in both namespaces.
Not applicable; this is the initial registration.

section.t: There are no additional security considerations other than those normally associated with the use and resolution of URNs in general, which are described in Functional Requirements for Uniform Resource Names and Uniform Resource Names (URNs).

section.title: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document adds a new entry ("mplify") in the urn-namespace registry. This is the defining document. When published, the entry can be found in the "Uniform Resource Names (URN) Namespaces" registry available from the IANA site (https://www.iana.org) and any associated mirrors.
